The files in this folder are data of the WSL Institute for Snow and
Avalanche Research SLF (www.slf.ch), measured by its IMIS stations and
published through its measurement service, https://measurement-api.slf.ch,
under Creative Commons CC BY 4.0,
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, as its data service's page
says: https://www.slf.ch/en/services-and-products/slf-data-service/. They
are not covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-22 from
https://measurement-api.slf.ch/public/api/imis/, without a key, with curl,
one GET each. The answers hold no personal data and no key.

    stations.json   GET /stations                 31,345 bytes, whole and
                    asked at 08:09:08 UTC         unchanged: 207 stations,
                                                  205 in Switzerland and 2
                                                  in Liechtenstein

    measurements.json                             CUT from the answer to
                    GET /measurements             GET /measurements, asked
                    asked at 08:09:08 UTC         at the same second, which
                                                  was 3,302,282 bytes: 9,639
                                                  rows of 203 stations, the
                                                  half hours from 08:30 UTC
                                                  on 2026-11-21 to 07:30 or
                                                  08:00 UTC on 2026-11-22

The answer is one JSON array written on one line, a flat object a row.
measurements.json keeps the rows whose station_code is one of DAV1
(Chrachenhorn), FAE1 (Albristhorn), GLA2 (Guppen), LAG2 (Tscheppa), MAN1
(Männlichen), MLB1 (Spitz) and WFJ2 (Weissfluhjoch), every one of their
rows, in the answer's order, each byte for byte as the service wrote it,
joined by commas between "[" and "]" as in the answer: 333 rows, 112,815
bytes. They were chosen for what they show: a wind station on a ridge
whose anemometer gave nothing (FAE1), a snow station without an anemometer
(LAG2) and one without a thermometer (GLA2), stations in the first
region's box and in the western one, Liechtenstein. The cut was made by a
script that split the array between "},{" and checked that every piece
read as JSON is the row of the whole answer it was cut from.

    openapi.json    GET https://measurement-api.slf.ch/openapi.json
                    whole and unchanged, 14,341 bytes: the service's own
                    description, which gives the unit of every value. A
                    test reads the units from it.

The folder evening/ holds three answers of the service's history of one
station, whole and unchanged, asked at 08:11:12 UTC:

    evening/STATION.json   GET /station/STATION/measurements
                           ?period_in_days=7

for DAV1, WFJ2 and MLB1: 336 half hours each, from 08:30 UTC on
2026-11-15 to 08:00 UTC on 2026-11-22, in the same form as the rows of
/measurements. The adapter does not ask for histories. They are here for
the next two files.

stations_evening.json and measurements_evening.json are NOT answers of
the service as it gave them. They are a sample for the server's
development mode, whose clock stands at 19:05 UTC on 2026-11-18, four
days before this source was recorded; /measurements answers with the last
24 hours only and cannot be asked for an earlier moment.

    stations_evening.json      stations.json cut to DAV1, WFJ2 and MLB1,
                               each object byte for byte, in the
                               answer's order
    measurements_evening.json  the rows of evening/STATION.json from
                               2026-11-17T19:30:00Z to
                               2026-11-18T18:30:00Z, byte for byte, the
                               stations in the order DAV1, MLB1, WFJ2 as
                               /measurements orders them: 47 rows each

So every value in the sample is one the service gave, for the station and
the half hour it says. The newest is of 18:30 UTC: at 08:09 UTC on
2026-11-22 half of the stations had a value of 08:00 and half of 07:30,
so the value of 19:00 is not taken to have been there at 19:05. What the
service answered at that moment is not known. A test of this crate holds
the sample against the histories.

stations_damaged.json and measurements_damaged.json are not the service's
data: they are the evening sample with things changed by hand, to test
how the adapter reports what it cannot read. The test that uses them says
what was changed.

To record them again: fetch /stations and /measurements in one go and
replace the two files, cut the second as above; set the moment in
tests/pipeline.rs; run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review
what changed. The counts the tests pin will differ. The evening sample
stays as it is for as long as the development mode's clock does; should
the clock move, make it again from histories asked within seven days of
the new moment, as above.

A value in these files is what an instrument reported. It is no statement
that a place can be flown.
